analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes: docs/architecture/inference.md (MTP idle-upgrade staging, drain and commit; typical-acceptance MTP; sampling defaults; native MiMo and Qwen4 admission; coordinator-serving channels) and docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md (date bump plus a paragraph separating startup calibration from profile qualification). No source, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage code changes, so no threat-model controls are weakened.

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
- inference.md ~L508-519 documents typical MTP acceptance as default for sampled rows. This is approximate rather than distribution-exact output. The doc states it is not a qualified quality claim, which is consistent with T-007 and T-056 (no correctness or runtime-secrecy guarantees).
- inference.md ~L608-609 says the sampler is not part of prompt or cache identity, so SSD cache identity is unchanged. This is compatible with T-041; a code pass should confirm no cache-key or AAD changes accompany the doc.
- inference.md ~L944-946 states the in-memory video asset never writes the payload to disk, consistent with T-050.
- inference.md ~L1029-1031 says the provider encrypts SSE frames back over the coordinator connection and starts no local HTTP endpoint, consistent with T-008.
- The MTP drain/idle-upgrade text (L423-448) describes admission fencing with 503 slot_state rejections and no force-cancel of accepted work. This relates to T-010 and T-029 availability, but it is a documentation claim only.

No security findings. The behavior described in the docs was not verified against code, which was not supplied.
